title: fix(app-shell): the Automations rail stops telling a flow with a declared trigger that it has "no trigger" (objectui#11281)
body:
Fixes #11281
Clause-②: no

Studio's Automations rail no longer tells a flow that declares a trigger that it has "no trigger". For a policy-unbound schedule flow, the status dot's title is now the platform's `reason`, verbatim. This delivers objectui#9217's ruling B (comment 5919298624) on the rail, as triage carried it (5921147097) and as PR objectui#11271 delivered it on the Setup page.

## Why

`FlowStatusDot` titled every enabled flow with `bound: false` "Enabled · no trigger (run manually)". The pillar's status map kept only `enabled` and `bound` from the `GET /api/v1/automation/_status` rows. `FlowRuntimeState` in the installed `@objectstack/spec` 17.5.0 says `bound` is false "for a flow with no declared trigger (manual / screen flows) AND for one whose declared trigger type has no registered trigger — `triggerType` distinguishes the two". On `reason` it says "`bound: false` alone cannot be read as a defect" and "Consumers RENDER it; ⛔ do not parse it". On a default deployment, every package-authored schedule flow reaches the rail as `enabled: true, bound: false, triggerType: 'schedule'` with a reason, and its author was told the flow has no trigger.

## What changed (all in `StudioDesignSurface.tsx`)

- **The status map.** It now keeps `triggerType` and `reason` beside `enabled` / `bound`, read from the same `_status` answer the pillar already fetched. A new `flowRailState` helper narrows each row: `triggerType` and `reason` are kept only when they are non-empty strings and are otherwise absent, the same way the engine omits them. This matches `joinPackagedFlows` in PR objectui#11271.
- **`FlowStatusDot`** titles an enabled, unbound flow by this table. Disabled and bound flows keep their titles.

| row | title |
|---|---|
| has a `reason` | the reason, verbatim. It is never parsed, compared or restyled |
| no `triggerType` (manual / screen flow, or any older backend) | `engine.studio.auto.onUnbound`, "no trigger (run manually)", as today |
| `triggerType` but no `reason` (a backend that predates `reason`) | the existing `engine.studio.auto.enabled`, "Enabled" |

- The visible text ("On") and the dot's colour follow `enabled` alone. Nothing gets `role=alert` or a destructive class.
- No locale key is added, no platform sentence is copied, and no dependency is added. The pillar's flow load and save paths (PR objectui#11296) are not touched.
- One changeset: `@object-ui/app-shell` patch.

## Measurements behind the design (dispatch Zone 2)

1. **Red first, reproduced.** Before any source edit, the new pins ran against the `origin/main` source (`5f2d9676c9`) and gave `Tests 4 failed | 7 passed (11)`. Through the real pillar, the policy flow's dot was titled `Enabled · no trigger (run manually)`. The controls (manual, bound, disabled) were green.
2. **How "no declared trigger" reads in `triggerType`.** PR objectui#11271 has no reading to copy. Its `FlowRuntimeStateRow` reads only `name`, `enabled` and `reason`, and its docblock says so. So the two cannot disagree. The reading used here is the contract's own: "Declared trigger type, when the flow declares one", so absent means no declared trigger. The producer matches. In objectstack's automation engine, `getFlowRuntimeStates()` sends `triggerType: resolved?.triggerType`. `resolveTriggerBinding` answers `undefined` for a manual or screen flow, which drops the key from JSON. Otherwise it answers one of `record_change`, `time_relative`, `schedule` or `api`. No `'manual'` or `'screen'` value is ever sent.
3. **A declared trigger with no `reason`.** Setup gives that row an "On" badge and nothing about binding. The rail says the same through the existing `engine.studio.auto.enabled` key, so no new key was needed. With the current producer the case cannot happen: `describeUnboundReason` returns a sentence on each of its branches for an enabled, unbound flow that declares a trigger. Only a backend that sends `triggerType` but predates `reason` reaches it.
4. **Older backend.** A row with neither field still gets "no trigger (run manually)". The existing tooltip test and the manual-flow control pin this.
5. **Text and styling.** "On" and the emerald dot are unchanged and pinned. Only the title moves.

## Pins

- `FlowStatusDot.test.tsx`, describe "a declared trigger the engine has not armed (objectui#11281)". A policy-unbound schedule flow's title equals its reason exactly, in en and zh, and is not the `onUnbound` text. The visible text is `engine.studio.auto.on`, the dot keeps its emerald class, and there is no alert and no destructive class. A flow with no `triggerType` still gets `onUnbound` (the control). A declared trigger without a reason gets `engine.studio.auto.enabled`. Bound and disabled flows keep `onBound` and `offTitle` (the controls). The assertions name locale keys, not English copy. The reason is fixture text, not a platform sentence.
- `StudioDesignSurface.railUnboundReason-11281.test.tsx` uses the real `AutomationsPillar` with a routing `_status` double that serves the rows in the engine's wire shape. The policy flow's rail dot is titled with the reason and still reads "On". The manual, bound and disabled rows keep their titles (the controls).

## Evidence (HEAD `dcf891b9e1`, every run after the final commit; heavy runs under `os-verify-lock`)

- **Ablation** with `ablation-replace.mjs` in WRAP mode, on the committed fix. The `triggerType` / `reason` spreads in `flowRailState` were replaced with a marker comment: anchor 1 to 0, blob `d3375d4afe46` to `705bdad20d7d`. Result: `Tests 1 failed | 10 passed (11)`. The one red test is the pillar's policy-flow pin. All `FlowStatusDot` unit pins and the pillar controls stayed green, so the pillar pin is the one that measures the map path. Restore proved: the blob equals HEAD `d3375d4afe46` and `git diff HEAD` is empty. The test imports its subject by relative path from source, so no dist preflight applies.
- `pnpm exec turbo run build --filter='@object-ui/app-shell^...' --concurrency=2`: `Tasks: 28 successful, 28 total`. Then `pnpm --filter @object-ui/app-shell type-check` (`tsc --noEmit && tsc -p tsconfig.test.json`) exited 0 with 0 `error TS`. The test project's `include` is `src/**/*.test.ts` plus `src/**/*.test.tsx`, which covers both test files.
- One vitest run covered `packages/app-shell/src/views/studio-design/` (84 files), `studio-locale.i18n.test.tsx`, `setup/PackagedAutomationPage.test.tsx` and `__tests__/spec-symbol-parity.test.ts`: `Test Files 87 passed (87)`, `Tests 551 passed (551)`. The run included every suite that `git grep` finds for `FlowStatusDot`, `getFlowRuntimeStates` or `automation/_status`.
- **Lint, narrowed.** `eslint --format json` ran from `packages/app-shell` (the package's `lint` population, under the root `eslint.config.js`) on the 3 changed source and test files: 3 files, 0 errors, 17 warnings. The same command on the base blob of `StudioDesignSurface.tsx` (through `--stdin`) gives 0 errors and the same 17 warnings as an identical multiset. The two test files are clean. The root config has no type-aware linting (no `parserOptions` or `projectService`), so the diff cannot move a verdict in an untouched file.
- These all exited 0: `pnpm check:i18n-keys`, `check:i18n-dead-keys`, `check:i18n-drift` (0 en values changed), `check:new-line-citations` (0 new), `node scripts/check-changeset-presence.mjs`, `pnpm changeset:check`, `check:control-bytes`, `check:changeset-claims`, `check:pending-changeset-literals`, `check:test-path-roots`, `check:vi-mock-specifiers`, `check:vi-mock-inherit`, `check:vi-mock-override-shape`, `check:spec-symbols`, and `node scripts/markdown-test-inputs.mjs --audit`.
- Not run locally: the full `pnpm test` and `pnpm lint` farm. That is left to CI.

## Acceptance notes

- With a `reason`, the title is the reason alone, with no "Enabled ·" prefix. This mirrors Setup, which pairs the "On" badge with the bare sentence. Adding a prefix would need a composed string or a new key, and the ruling asks for neither.
- The stray doc comment "Automations pillar — flows: list → FlowPreview" still sits above the `FlowRuntimeState` alias's own docblock. It is cosmetic and left alone.
